source_title: Bomb squad called to country town after reports of shot fired
source_excerpt:
Armed police were involved in the arrest of a 66-year-old man in Numurkah on Saturday. ( Supplied )
The bomb squad has been called to a northern Victorian property after a man allegedly fired a gun at a vehicle.
Victoria Police said investigators were told a man fired a gun towards a vehicle in Numurkah, two-and-a-half hours' drive north of Melbourne, on Thursday.
Detectives searched the property on Saturday and found a "suspicious device".
The Bomb Response Unit was called in and made the device safe.
The Victoria Police bomb squad was called to the residence after a suspicious device was located. ( Supplied )
Video seen by the ABC shows a shirtless man exiting a property and walking towards armed tactical police on Saturday.
The man lies face-down on the ground near heavily armed police before being arrested.
A police spokesperson said a 66-year-old man was arrested and charged with reckless conduct endangering serious injury and possessing and making an explosive substance.
He was also charged with possessing Victoria Police equipment without authority, cultivating and possessing cannabis, and possessing a prohibited weapon without exemption.
A police vehicle remained outside the property on Sunday morning.
The man was remanded to appear at the Shepparton Magistrates' Court tomorrow.
A Victoria Police vehicle remained at the Numurkah property on Sunday morning. ( ABC News: Andrew Mangelsdorf )
